findings.reason: the node would build a confirm step that cannot fail, leaving the release→confirm→cancel ordering's only safety property unverified, and §2's done-when lists no test that could catch it, so the plan must name a discriminating instrument (a completion fingerprint sent direct to the replacement's port) in the step and in its test list.
findings.text: §2's overlap sequence confirms the swap with "Confirm through the router's own `/v1/models` that the model now resolves to the new engine"; that instrument cannot answer the question, because `_serve_catalog` (`imas_ambix/agent/router.py:2284`) groups upstream cards by model id and, for the duplicate, emits only the card `_preferred_owner` selected, whose launch metadata (`validate_catalog_metadata`, `imas_ambix/agent/vllm_catalog.py:34`) is exactly `accelerator_family`, `accelerator_count` and `checkpoint_precision` — identical for two copies of one profile, and naming neither the job id nor a start stamp — so the response is the same before and after the release and §2's own deploy argument ("a hold is honoured only by a router started from the new code") is never actually observed; `imas_ambix/agent/AGENTS.md` §3b, the passage §2's overlap path reproduces, tells the two engines apart by a generation fingerprint for exactly this reason

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every anchor in §2 resolves: `generate_serve_script` (`imas_ambix/agent/slurm.py:432`, its `registry write` step at :863 ahead of the readiness loop), `ServeRegistration` (`imas_ambix/agent/registry.py:33`) and its `write`/`remove`/`publish` subcommands (:511-527 — no `release` yet, which §2 proposes adding), `_resolve_router_upstreams` (`imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:1507`) with both of its paths present (the registration loop and the scheduler-only loop), `LiveRoute.job_id` on the scheduler-only route so a held job is skippable by id (`cli.py:1446-1500`), `_preferred_owner`'s widest-then-later-start ranking (`imas_ambix/agent/router.py:1639`), `_running_jobs`' operator-scoped `squeue -u` (`cli.py:1219`), `shutdown`'s existing `--all` flag (`cli.py:1073`), `imas_ambix/agent/AGENTS.md` §2's core-ledger recipe and §3b's rotation passage, and `ops/lane-cycle/AGENTS.md`, the runbook the intro links.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2 declares its own negative control ("Removing the skip on either path fails its test, which is the negative control") and each of its six bullets names an observable outcome; the one measure §2 cannot fail is raised under reasoning instead.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the cycle's tests run in place on the fleet node, and the record lands in `lane-cycles.jsonl` beside the durable `lane.json`, not in a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §2 introduces `imas_ambix/agent/reload.py`, `--mode auto|overlap|pause`, `held_registrations` and `registry release`, none of which carries a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag, and no comment or docstring in §2 is changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2's overlap confirm step reads the router's `/v1/models`, which cannot distinguish the replacement from the engine it replaces, so that step passes whether or not the release took effect.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one deliverable, the overlap path of `agent restart`, with its two supporting edits (held registration, `shutdown` refuse-on-two) named as work items inside it rather than as separate goals.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §2's `data-links` to `hot-reload-the-serve#s1` resolves, followup `f-hrs-001` carries the §1-then-§2 order its own text states, and s3 declares `data-status="deferred"` consistently with §3's "This section is deferred".
